Star Wars: Jedi Fallen Order offers three core elements: A) a combat-mobility inspired by the likes of Jedi Academy or Outcast. You have access to abilities that let you leap over your opponents to slash them in the back, double jump to avoid AOE damage, and walls to run across into a take-down. With this mobility, however, comes the importance of timing! Timing is tremendously important in this game, especially when confronting several enemies with ranged and melee weapons or bosses that attack relentlessly. Now with respect to combat, expect B) the parry sequences and optional difficulty of Dark Souls: the hardest difficulty setting "Jedi Grand Master" is essentially the "prepare to die" mode. Depending upon your difficulty setting, parry openings and enemy attack speed will differ. Thirdly, it offers C) the free-roam exploration and puzzles of a game like Tomb Raider. These three elements are combined surprisingly well, moreover, with a few minor animation hiccups here and there. This isn't a KOTOR or JK4 - but that is fine. It stands on its own as a unique and great addition to the Star Wars franchise. The story is engaging, the characters are unique and well-developed, and the collectible customization options are a nice touch. This is a GREAT precedent to set for EA, as a single-player experience. It is, at the moment, free of the greed previously characteristic of EA. Therefore I say: Well done, EA and Respawn! I give Fallen Order a solid 9/10!

Jedi Fallen Order is, by quite a big margin, the most surprising title of the year for me, not only compared to the expectations I had for it, which were admittedly pretty low, but for how genuinely brilliant this game achieves to be.

It's true, Fallen Order really looks like a greatest hits of all the major and most appreciated mechanics we've seen in single player videogames in the last few years: we have bombastic cinematic moments took straight from the Uncharted series (if you played Uncharted 2, you'll probably find the first hour of the game to be hilarious, in that sense), tombs with puzzles to solve and walls to jump onto that seem borrowed from the rebooted Tomb Raider trilogy, a combat system very similar to what we recently saw in Sekiro by From Software but, thankfully, they never end up falling in the "been there, done that" zone and they always feel extremely polished and cohesively combined, returning us a fantastic experience that is far more than the sum of its parts. 

The level design by Respawn is also top notch, with an intricate map design that is both a joy to explore in every corner the first time, in order to find secrets and hidden optional enemies, and fun to return to once you unlocked those abilities you were missing and that you can now use to reach places you couldn't get to before. The difficulty is well balanced and, at the hardest setting, it gives you a nice challenge without resulting too frustrating: this is definitely the difficulty to pick if you're experienced with action games like Sekiro. The story is coherent and serviceable, enriched by a cast of interesting characters you'll most likely want to know more about (sadly our main guy isn't one of them, that is the one thing that never changed from my initial impressions). On the technical side the game is also very solid, with great graphics and an extremely polished PC port; the only issues I encountered during my playthrough were all due to the integration with Origin, which is something they really can't drop soon enough. 

All things considered, Star Wars: Jedi Fallen Order is a brilliant game that everyone should at least consider playing, even if they're not particularly interested in the Star Wars universe (I'm not a massive fan of the saga myself). Great job, Respawn!

Jedi Fallen Order is a very good action/adventure game that takes place between the 3rd and 4th star wars movie. You will play a padawan who survived order 66 and will try to rebuild the jedi order while being hunted by inquisitors.

The gameplay is very good with a well done adventure/loot aspect. You will be able to explore several planets in order to find some improvements for your equipment, but mainly skins. There is also a complete skill tree, allowing you to unlock passive perks or new attacks. You will also unlock different lightsaber stances as you progress through the game. The fights are very good, they are quite aggressive, so you will need to have good reflexes. The bosses are quite strong depending on the difficulty of the game but still very enjoyable to do, especially if you like souls like or games like god of war.

The story is very good, there are many references to the universe in general and the plot is very cool to follow, the cinematics are well placed and well done. You might not understand everything if you are not familiar with the universe but the game tries to put you in the right context from the start.

One of the bad things about this game in my opinion is the level design and the use of the map. You will have to go back to your ship very often and since there is no fast travel, it is very easy to get lost while trying to reach it.

In conclusion, I recommend this very good game to any fan of the star wars universe but also to anyone who wants an adventure game with an entertaining story and provides a good challenge. The game is not very expensive on steam and it's well worth the price.

[h1]Overview[/h1]
[b]Jedi Fallen Order[/b] (SWJFO) is an [b]hybrid action-adventure title[/b] that combines gameplay elements from various popular genres, ultimately creating its own custom blend of mechanics. In this game players impersonate Cal Kestis, a former Jedi apprentice now gone into hiding after the infamous Order 66 was executed. Soon he has to abandon a cover-up job, after an accident puts Inquisition agents on his tracks, from here his journey begins to discover not only ancient mysteries, also his own true nature.

SWJFO plays out as a [b]blend of mechanics from mostly Souls-like and Metroidvania genres[/b]: combat heavily inspires to the former, putting [b]great emphasis on learning enemy attack patterns, dodging at the right times, parrying enemy attacks[/b] just before they land in order to stun them (as seen in [i]Sekiro[/i]), plus also using Force Powers preferably in clever manners to gain the upper hand. The metroidvania part becomes prominent in exploration, with platforming / jumping sections and also with several areas of each planet being gated off until Cal acquires more powers or technologies - this [b]encourages backtracking in a good way[/b], to find secrets, items and even whole optional areas or bosses.

The game is not exempt from issues though: the [b]lack of any fast-travel means between "bonfires" makes backtracking to find every secret quite annoying[/b] especially in more complex maps. Secondly, [b]some force powers combos or skills are too powerful[/b], such as Lv.3 force push being able to slam enemy groups and sometimes even bosses into pitfalls. Lastly, [b]character progression is watered down[/b] with no attribute system, no "real" gear to find and no consumables apart from Stims - those wanting deeper character development possibilities will be disappointed. [b]Also, some plot holes or sudden character behavior changes happen[/b], especially later on, for no good reason. 

[b]Overall, Jedi Fallen Order is a really solid action-adventure game[/b] that faithfully recreates the Star Wars universe with incredible visuals, delivers consistent fun gameplay mechanics, decent story, and extreme challenge on the highest difficulty setting for those seeking a punishing experience. [b]It took me 20 hours to gather most secrets, fully explore every planet, and complete the game on Jedi Master difficulty - for the proposed price of 60€, no replay value but also excellent overall quality of content, I can suggest buying full price to Star Wars and/or Souls-like fans, while players less passionate about these genres could wait for a sale instead.[/b]

[h1]Pros & Cons[/h1]

🔵 [b]Pros[/b]
+ Incredible visuals and art direction recreating the Star Wars universe faithfully, ensuring excellent immersion.
+ Well designed mix of genres that ultimately works well, delivering challenging combat and interesting exploration.
+ Decent storyline and characters, not as much "Disneyfied" as initially expected, though not stellar it does the job.
+ Extreme challenge on Grandmaster difficulty, on par if not harder than Sekiro, and definitely harder than Dark Souls.
+ The great quantity of secret areas, collectibles, lore entries and cosmetics will please completionists.

🔴 [b]Cons[/b]
- Character progression system is not very deep, without custom build possibilities or detailed attribute control. 
- No fast travel between "bonfires" makes it annoying to backtrack already cleared areas over and over to get to new ones. 
- Mandatory use of Origin Client even if the game is purchased on Steam.
- You cannot dismember human enemies such as stormtroopers, which is immersion-breaking and quite stupid.
- Double lightsaber is inferior to the single one and there really is no point in using it.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1915823828

[h1]In-Depth Breakdown[/h1]

🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis[/b]
The gameplay of SWJFO is divided into Exploration, Character Management and Combat. 

[b]Exploration[/b] is performed on foot, and progressively with the aid of various Force Powers such as wall running, double-jump and more. One of the core elements in this game's exploration is that several zones are initially barred to the player, accessible only later when Cal gained the correct force power or droid modification for BD-1. This mechanic promotes meaningful backtracking and it is really worth it doing so since other than cosmetics and lore entries, invaluable Stim Crates (Estus), the only way to increase the maximum quantity of heals, are almost only found in secret areas - exploration of such areas becomes a necessity on higher difficulties. Each planet is littered with meditation circles (bonfires), where players can spend skill points and replenish their Stims and health at the cost of respawning all enemies, they also will go back at the last circle used if defeated. The fact all hidden crates only deliver cosmetics since there is not an equip system kinda makes exploration less worth in this sense, especially for those not interested in cosmetics. 

[b]Character Management[/b] mainly consists in spending skill points at a circle to acquire passive skills and active combos, or upgrade existing force powers. The skill tree branches threefold, with Lightsaber, Force and Survival areas, each giving out respectively advanced combos (not very useful mostly), upgraded force powers and capacity, and higher max health or better defensive skills. For the rest, customizing Cal and BD-1's appearance and making your own lightsaber are cool features, though only for the sake of fashion.

[b]Combat[/b] plays out in a faster paced manner compared to Dark Souls and focuses more on perfect parrying enemy blows rather than dodging or rolling, which are two different things in this game. There is no stamina for dodging or using basic attacks, however there is for blocking, there is Force which acts as MP, and is replenished by damaging, perfect parrying enemies, or with a late-game stim passive. Parrying enemy blows will stun them, enabling powerful counterattacks, this needs to be done multiple times for stronger foes and many times for bosses. This mechanic, unlike in Sekiro is not mandatory, as there are many other ways to damage foes, one of the most prominent being analyzing their patterns and understanding when they cannot block your blows after a specific attack or combo, and strike at that time. Force Powers are a big deal in combat especially later on, enabling quick defeat of enemy groups by, for example, pushing them all into a pitfall. Dodging an enemy blow at the last second performs a perfect dodge, enabling a counterattack as well in most cases, useful for unblockable attacks. Generally enemies hurt a lot (On Jedi Master and above) and can even stun-lock you into flurries of blows, there is a high punish level for failed dodges or parries.

🔩 [b]Performance Analysis[/b]
[u]PC Specs: RTX2080Ti, Ryzen 3900X, 32GB RAM DDR4[/u]
The game runs without issues on this config and presents no stability or technical problems. The optimization is reportedly very good for the graphics delivered, with Dynamic Resolution playing an important part in getting good frame-rates on lower end systems while having good visual fidelity. You will need at least an average machine by today's standards to run this game without issues.

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
Jedi Fallen Order is an excellent action-adventure game that successfully blends mechanics belonging to different genres, offering an experience most action, souls-like and Star Wars fans will enjoy.

[h1]Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order[/h1]
I’ll be honest — I’ve never watched a single Star Wars movie before playing Jedi: Fallen Order. I barely knew who the Jedi even were. But despite that, this game completely drew me in and made me curious about the entire Star Wars universe.

From the start, Fallen Order impressed me with its cinematic storytelling and emotional depth. Cal Kestis’ journey felt relatable even without knowing the broader lore. The way the game slowly unveils his past and trauma kept me hooked, and the bond with BD-1? Instant favorite. The world-building, characters, and set pieces all felt so grand and immersive that I didn’t feel left out — instead, I felt pulled in.

Gameplay-wise, it’s a satisfying blend of exploration, puzzle-solving, and Souls-like combat. The lightsaber combat is incredibly fun, and using the Force powers just never gets old. The level design reminded me of Metroidvania-style games, with a real sense of reward for backtracking and unlocking new paths.

What’s wild is that by the end of the game, I actually wanted to watch the movies and learn more about this galaxy far, far away. Jedi: Fallen Order didn’t just entertain me — it turned me into a curious fan of a franchise I had ignored for years.

You don’t need to be a Star Wars expert to enjoy this game. It stands strong on its own, but it also opens the door to a much bigger universe. Now, I’ve got a watchlist full of Star Wars content — all thanks to one game.

Preface: Before I start, I want to state that I belong to the group of people who thinks that whatever EA comes up with is bad. This is especially so in the aftermath of the horrendous mtx system that STAR WARS Battlefront II has implemented. Thus, I tend to shy away from EA games. However, the gameplay I saw and reviews I heard from people who tried this game for the first time gave me a better sense of the game and on an impulse, I bought it. The best part is, I don't regret it.

Fallen Order is a very Sekiro-style game where it relies heavily on deflecting, dodging and parrying attacks in order to get some of your own in. Throughout the game you'll earn force abilities which allow you to traverse the map more freely and explore certain locations, yielding upgrades to your characters. This means that certain parts of the map will be inaccessible at first, and that you may have to come back later to get the loot within said parts. You'll also encounter locked doors which act as shortcuts similar to Souls-like games.

Combat is fluid and satisfying. Wielding a lightsaber, you can deflect melee attacks and blaster bolts back at enemies. Enemies have stamina bars and when depleted, allows you to perform a finisher move. These moves are super satisfying to watch as you see Cal expertly eviscerates his opponents. (There are no dismemberment for human enemies, only beasts). However, enemies stagger you like there's no tomorrow and hence it is very important to take out the more annoying ones. Even the lowliest beast or stormtrooper will stagger you and open you to the more dangerous attacks performed by other enemy types, speaking of which, there is no lack of. It is very similar to Sekiro and if you like its swordplay, you will like Fallen Order.

Movement is a strong feature of this game. It is reminiscent of the Tomb Raider and Uncharted Series. Cal can climb on vines, wallrun, double jump etc. These movement abilities all help you to reach areas that provide upgrades to Cal and his droid. Additionally, puzzles exist in this game similar to the tombs in the aforementioned games and such movement abilities are paramount to solving these puzzles.

Graphics are pretty good, with a emphasis on cinematic cutscenes. Customisation of your ship, Cal, the droid, your lightsaber exists and can be found throughout the entire game. [spoiler]WITH NO MICROTRANSACTIONS[/spoiler] Story seems pretty generic but I'm only a few hours in and have yet to complete the first planet. Controls are bindable with controller support as well. I have yet to encounter bugs but I do get random frame drops. However, it's nothing game-breaking.

All in all, I am amazed. Like many others, I was highly sceptical of the game before it launched but now I can safely say that it is worth its price. Respawn has done a very good job of redeeming EA.

[h1]The Best Star Wars Game in 10 Years[/h1]

That is my current opinion. It's not perfect, but it's damn good.

[b] Summary [/b]

This game had a great story, and looks amazing, but where it really shines is in the game-play. Upon watching for the first time, I was very underwhelmed with how it looked, however, after playing you really realize how smooth and fun the combat is. I barely noticed the weird animations, and every time I got in a fight, I was excited to test my skills. 

The game offers nothing really [i]new[/i] with it's mechanics, but it's a perfect combination of the game-mechanics we've seen for the last few years, and you can definitely compare it to all sorts of existing titles.

The way the story flows is not as linear as you think either. It plays out a lot like Super Mario Odyssey. You have a ship and you can choose which planets you got to. You have entire planets to explore and find all of it's chests and secrets. There is lot's of climbing around and solving puzzles as well, Tomb-Raider style. I think the balance is perfect however.

Building your own lightsaber is very cool. We've seen this before in Jedi Academy, but this game allows you to select each an every part. You will continually find more parts as you explore as well, including materials for the lightsaber. It really does get you more invested in the character as you personalize his saber.

Unfortunately as for clothing, and your looks in general you don't have a lot of options. The only real cosmetic is your poncho. You will find lot's of poncho styles and colors, but I did not play using a poncho ever because I personally think it looks dumb.

[b] Pro [/b]

These pros are my absolute favorite things about the game

[list]
[*]  Lightsaber Customization
[*] Combat
[*] Story
[*] Worlds are different and unique
[*] Characters
[*] Overall fun is extreme
[/list]

[b] Con [/b]

These cons may get nit-pickey, as there is not a lot wrong with the game in my opinion.

[list]
[*] Too short, really leaves you wanting more, and it ends right as things start to pick up
[*] Frame drops (specs below)
[*] I don't want to wear a damn poncho
[*] No replay-ability, once you beat it, you can uninstall
[*] Would have liked more things to do on your ship, since it acts as your hub. 
[/list]

[b] Conclusion [/b]

In conclusion, this game is overall outstanding. I think this will go down as a classic in the future and I look forward to a bigger, better sequel or some high-end DLC. I think what would [b]really[/b] keep this game going in the future, they need to add something that would keep players around. I think simple level-creator would do the trick. Players could sandbox in it, or even share levels on the workshop. That however is just my thoughts on the matter.

[h1] [b]Overall Score:[/b] 8.5 / 10 [/h1]

Buy this game if you are a Star Wars fan. You won't regret it. This is so much better than The Force Unleashed, and you DO NOT want to miss this experience.

Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order was an absolute blast to play through, so much that I even went the extra mile to 100% the game. I have a lot of positive things to say about this game as well as some negatives which could easily be fixed. This is by far the best single player Star Wars game we've gotten in years or perhaps even the best single player Star Wars game of all time? That's of course up for you to decide.

[h1] Pro: [/h1]
1. The game has a very cinematic feel to it. It's like you could take a screenshot at any moment and it would look like you're in the middle of a cinematic.

2. Combat feels very natural and is quite fast paced if you build your character for it.

3. You constantly get showered in new upgrade points, new cosmetics for you, your ship and your companion droid. It always felt nice to unlock something new even though the customization in this game diesn't amazing.

4. Enemies are quite fair and balanced but punish you if never block and attempt to spam attack them

5. There's an easy mode option for those who's not really into the whole souls like games. This difficulty is so easy that dying becomes nearly impossible. Just wanted to bring this up since some people might just wanna enjoy the story and gameplay without the challenge.

6. The game's story feels important enough to keep you going. While I was invested in the story it certainly wasn't insanely impressive. It was a good story that was easy to follow and it didn't overstay its welcome.

[h1] Cons: [/h1]
1. Unfortunately there's no fast travel system in the game and honestly it really hurts when you have to backtrack for the 10th time going through a +10 minute platformer section before arriving at your desired location.

2. The game doesn't utilize the Star Wars franchise all that well when it comes to locations. You see all the planets are rather plain compared to locations you'll see in for example Star Wars The Clone Wars. Dathomir was the only planet that really stood out. I'm not saying the world doesn't have that Star Wars feel, it's just the choice of planets were too basic. I would've loved to see a planet like Umbara.

3. Traversing through the map feels amazing once you've unlocked all the powerups but prior to unlocking all the powerups it feels like something's missing. I'm not against power growth but it feels sluggish at times early game.

4. The force can be a bit buggy and so can the AI. I experienced alien lifeforms, critters, stormtroopers, and even once a boss glitching parsely through the ground doing combat. It doesn't despawn them and they do jump up from the ground when attacking but it can look a bit derpy. You can force pull vines and a lot of the time I'd pull a vine to me but my character refuses to grab onto it.

[h1] Conclusion: [/h1]
While the game definitely has it's pros and cons the good just outweighs the bad. When I first started playing Fallen Order I wanted to give the game a solid 10/10 but as I played through it the cracks began to show. My final rating for Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a solid 8/10. If you're a Star Wars fan you should definitely give this game a chance.

Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order is a third person action game set between Revenge of the Sith and Rogue One. The player controls Cal Kestis, a Jedi who went into hiding after surviving Order 66 as a Padawan, and must now go on a quest to try to rebuild the Jedi Order.

[h1]The Good[/h1]

•	Using my lightsaber and force powers in combat made me feel like a powerful Jedi. Force pushing enemies to send them flying off a cliff never stops being fun, you can also pull them towards you, slow their movement so they can’t block your attacks, throw your lightsaber at mid-range enemies and kill distant enemies by deflecting their blaster bolts back at them.

•	Several different enemy types including Stormtroopers and other Imperial soldiers armed with blasters, shock batons, rocket launchers and flamethrowers, wildlife, giant monsters, droids, AT-ST walkers, and Sith wielding their own lightsabers and force powers.

•	Combat is challenging on Jedi Master difficulty (the third of four difficulty levels). Regular enemies feel nicely balanced and are fun to fight, and sometimes you can take advantage of Stormtroopers and wildlife attacking each other, but let’s just say the bosses are not messing around and will have you wishing you could turn to the dark side. Be prepared to die a few times while you learn their attack patterns. One thing I liked about the boss design though is they’re mostly 1v1 fights so they feel like epic showdowns against important characters, instead of the usual video game bosses where you spend most of the time fighting a bunch of respawning minions.

•	The story is interesting, arguably better than some of the recent films, and voice acting is good. Cal’s droid ally BD-1 has as much personality as R2-D2 or BB-8.

•	Music and sound effects of lightsabers and blasters feels like Star Wars.

•	Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.

[h1]The Bad[/h1]

•	I frequently encountered terrible stutters which dropped my framerate (which otherwise was a solid 60) for a couple of seconds at a time into the 30’s, and occasionally even into single digits. I think its related to loading assets because it mostly happens while moving between areas and sometimes during cutscenes when approaching a planet. Thankfully it didn’t happen much during combat. Compared to the recommended specs on the store page, my CPU (i7 6700K) and RAM (16GB) are equal and my graphics card is better (GTX 1080). A quick look on the forums shows several lengthy threads about the same problem, so this seems to be a common complaint.

[h1]The Recommendation[/h1]

Jedi Fallen Order is a must play for Star Wars fans because of high quality combat and story, but the technical problems are bad enough for me to recommend waiting for a sale.

I'm as shocked as anyone that EA published an actual good game this year.  Then again, FO76 is a crapshow, Obsidian broke out with TOW, and nothing makes much sense in the industry right now.

This game is fantastic.  The action is solid, level design is worth exploring without being frustrating (save for a few really odd puzzles here and there), the characters are well written, well animated, and well acted.  The story is better than expected, and, lo and behold, there are no microtransactions, none of the things I've disliked in the industry as of late.

I'm not even a Star Wars fan and I've enjoyed the heck out of this.  I got ~30 hours out of it, and it was worth all of that.

[h1] Story: I expected more 2/5[/h1]
Maybe I just expected too much, but I expected a AAA Single-Player-only-RPG , to have a deeper, more interesting story. And a [spoiler] much longer marked Story or at least some side- quests[/spoiler]
Maybe I am just pampered by Mass Effect, The Witcher and other more "story over gameplay" RPGs.
Character progression is nonexistent other than in the player character, dialogue is uninteresting and doesn't really motivate to click on the "talk" prompt more often. It is funny that [spoiler] the characters I bonded the most with, were BD-1: a droid who I (I the player, not Cal Kestis) can barely understand, Prauf: who gets (figuratively) negative screentime, and Merrin, the last character to be introduced [/spoiler]
I basically just went to where the pointer sent me to, doing stuff because "sure, it makes sense". But was never really motivated to go to progress the story, or to know what happens next.
It is kinda disappointing, since writing an Expanded Universe Star Wars story is almost storytelling with cheat codes. You have an already established Universe. The story doesn’t have to explain what a Jedi a Sith or the Force is. It doesn’t have to tell what happened in Order 66, because everyone and their grandmother knows.


[h1] Exploration: Starts Big and Beautiful, stalls at the end 3/5[/h1]
The world and the graphics are gorgeus, no way around it. I tried to find every secret and every upgrade in the first worlds, only to be stopped by my lack of abilities to progress. AS the game carries on, you learn new tricks and unlock new skills, which allow you to keep exploring worlds you thought you had explored completly. You can get lost in the bigger maps, and not always know if you have been here before or not.
A big downside is the lack of variety between maps, they all feel empty after a while, it basically boils down to empty[spoiler] grass planet[/spoiler], empty [spoiler] desert planet[/spoiler], empty [spoiler] ice planet[/spoiler]. 
This is especially noticeable the more you traverse the levels. In fact, it became so jarring when I watched my buddy start a new game, and the tutorial level felt more alive than the other ones.
The biggest problem is: [spoiler] 
At least after arriving in Kashyyyk, you will notice that the whole exploration will never reward you asides from some extra Stims, but the rest is basically just cosmetics. And not even good cosmetics. Different Paintjobs for the same model of BD-1, Mantis and Poncho. Sure, tinkering with your Lightsaber is cool and all, but the most important aspect of it, the colour, you will unlock as part of the story. And there are so many shades of brown, silver and black I will paint my saber before getting bored.
[/spoiler].
In the last three levels, I gave up on exploring, instead going directly to the main objective to do what the game does best…

[h1] Combat Gameplay: Now here is the good stuff 5/5[/h1]
Just to get it out of the way, this isn't Dark Souls, nor is it a soulslike. Sure, we have the dodge roll and parries, the [strike] Bonfire [/strike] Meditation, and we have limited healing with no regenerating health.
Alas, we don't have stamina managment, build paths which considerably change the way you approach combat. There is no: [i]managing your stats, equipment weight and rings to mantain fast-roll while still being able to cast Tears of denial if you put the Priestesses Ring on AND be able to one hand the claymore. [/i]
Fallen Order is not a soulslike and thats a good thing. Not every sword wielding 3rd Person action-adventure game has to be a soulslike.

In this game we have finally gotten a fair representation of the lightsaber. Clonetroopers absolutely melt like butter if you score a good hit. The enemies you can't just slice in two have good reasons to, they have weapons with which they parry your attacks, and should you catch them from behind, or break their poise, they will melt like butter too.
The 3D layout of the levels, and using the force powers you are more comfortable with greatly enhances the variety of the combat:
 [i]Do you go around and get rid of the ranged units? 
Or do you hide behind cover, and let melee units come to you?
Do you use your force powers to quickly get rid of the stronger units?
Or will you juggle the weaker enemies around, to then 1v1 the stronger ones? [/i]
[spoiler] Strong Force-pull into instakill stab is OP[/spoiler].
Whenever I died, and had to clear the way once again from the last checkpoint, I never saw it as a chore, and the combat never got boring.


One thing that bothered me, was the lack of specialization. Sure, you have a skill tree you where you can kinda built your playstyle around, but I could pick up any character at any point of the story, not knowing their skill tree, and barely notice a difference in combat. However, this is more something that bothered me because I expected the game to have it, and the combat system works perfectly without it.

Now is the game challenging? Yes, it is challenging and sometime frustrating, which isn’t for everyone I guess.
For a final comparison with Souls, I would summarize it like this:
 [i]Getting ganked by 5 enemies and surviving in Dark Souls makes me feel relief and accomplishment
Getting ganked by 10 enemies and surviving in Fallen Order makes me feel FUN AND TOTALLY BADASS[/i]
[h1] Non-Combat Gameplay: Some Force-Puzzles, that’s it 1/5[/h1]
Asides from exploration, which has some major problems, the non-combat gameplay are only 2 or 3 Force-Power-Puzzles which while not too hard, feel out of place. It feels like the devs saw the Tomb Raider Reboot Optional Tombs, and said “we want that, but with Force Powers and non-optional”
One could argue that the Garden is a series of Fetch-Quests, but I wouldn’t say that is peak Side-Quest-Material.
[h1] Summary[/h1]
Fallen Order, while being a step in a good direction, is a missed opportunity. Amazing graphics, almost perfect combat that doesn’t get boring, very polished gameplay (didn’t have a single issue in 25h) empty shell of a short story. No replay value at all.
I recommend getting it at a Steam Sale, I got it for 16 € and it seems a fair price.
Respawn Entertainment made a game which shows a lot of potential, and I am very excited to see them either making a sequel, or a spinoff, with hopefully better story and content, but the same amazing gameplay.

There’s always a game that reminds you of multiple games mixed as one. And Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order isn’t a poles apart case. It depicts a blend between popular games like Death Stranding, Tomb Raider and Dark Souls/Sekiro. The stunning and highly detailed graphics from death stranding, smooth and player-friendly movement from tomb raider and overall challenging gameplay from Dark Souls and Sekiro. Each progressing level adds more fun to the overall game.

[h1][b] 📝Story without spoilers:[/b][/h1]
There’s always a game that reminds you of multiple games mixed as one. And Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order isn’t a poles apart case. It depicts a blend between popular games like Death Stranding, Tomb Raider, and Dark Souls/Sekiro. The stunning and highly detailed graphics from Death Stranding, smooth and player-friendly movement from Tomb Raider and overall challenging gameplay from Dark Souls and Sekiro. Each progressing level adds more fun to the overall game.
  
[h1][b]🎮Gameplay:[/b][/h1]
The gameplay was truly amazing and engaging at each step. One of the best beginning mission that sucks you up in the action-packed gameplay. A normal day of metal scrapping and boom suddenly you are hanging from a floating ship, sliding through demolishing ship and falling into the mouth of a giant monster, and not just that, when you somehow evade the death, now you are getting attacked by the dark force. Does this excite you too? Well, then you should be ready with your gear to experience this madness. 

[b]Controls and Skill Tree[/b]
Now for the deep-dive review, controls were smooth and easy to remember. However, the skill tree only includes attack variety or increasing health and force cap. You might end up with 30+ combos executable from the same buttons. It’s not too distracting as most players just stick to the same combos for the rest of the game, but interesting enough to grind and unlock. Apart from the skill tree, you also unlock controls at certain segments of the playthrough that help you revisit the planets and overcome the blocked paths.

[b]Playthrough parameters[/b]
Even though you have free will to visit any available planet, some of them are very linear. They are not open-world at all. Instead, they work as a web of paths fused together in challenging enemy wave clear areas. Not only that, it restricts you to explore further paths if you haven’t unlocked the required skill. This aspect is mostly player dependent. Some might feel the urge to progress and complete story missions in order to return to the same planet and step forward for exploration. But players like me might get annoyed, as we want to conquer the task fully before stepping on to the furthermore lands. Navigation was another tedious task. They were fulfilling the purpose, but goddamn it gets overly confusing when you are required to travel through a path inter-joined at 3 different altitudes. Even though the game reveals secret hidden paths and shortcuts, while you are approaching your destination. Being at the border of the map and required to go all the way back to the ship was a nightmare.

[b]Enemies and Presentation[/b]
Cinematography literally bangs! Wide-angle captures of a gigantic structure or creature make you say wow. Level designing is surely a strong suit. Each level imposes a specific theme ranging from tropical forest, barren lands, and top facilities. Tropical theme was one of my favourite planet to traverse and find hidden chests. It was so humongous and can definitely work as a baseline for future Tarzan game.

[h1][b]📷Graphics:[/b][/h1]
When I say they match the graphic level of Death Stranding, it means that’s an easy 10/10. A phenomenal showcase of rendering techniques that stands firm with the new-gen requirements. I tried really hard to find any leftover detailing on the map or interactives. But I am happy to say that each level was top-notch with near to no graphic failure. All the animations, player movements, especially the lightsaber, felt lively and boosted the immersive experience throughout the game. The only letdown for me was the same chest searching animation underwater. Now, as the cute little companion BD searches the loot chests for me, which results in shaking of the chest. But underwater, when you try to loot a chest, our BD doesn’t enter the chest. Instead, it stays on our shoulder, and the loot chest shakes itself. It would have been a complete triumph if they fixed this graphic neglection.

[h1][b]📝Main Pros and Cons:[/b][/h1]

[b]Pros-[/b]
[list]
    [*]Amazing script and narration.
    [*]One of the best cinematography.
    [*]Top-notch graphics.
    [*]Linear yet immersive gameplay.
    [*]Each planet imposes sufficient amount of length and engaging puzzles.
    [*]XP requirement for skill tree is same for all.
[/list]

[b]Cons-[/b]
[list]
    [*]Overpriced if you don’t play through EA play as the story is not that long.
    [*]No replay value except the collectables.
    [*]Customization could have broaden up.
    [*]FPS drops.
[/list]

[h1][b]🏷️Tips to new players:[/b][/h1]
During the first planet mission, you will have an option to go with the campaign or visit a red planet. Go with the red planet (Dathomir) if you want duel wielding a lightsaber. It has multiple swings with less damage, but honestly, it looks super cool. Grinding for echoes is very fruitful as it increases your stem (health kit) capacity.

[h1][b]✉️Miscellaneous Information:[/b][/h1]
[b]Lightsaber-[/b]
Initially, you only have 3 colours to choose from, but after obtaining Kyber Crystal, you can unlock additional 5 colours. Blue, Green, Purple, Cyan, Magenta, Indigo, Yellow, Orange choose any that pleases your eyes.

[b]BD1 behavior-[/b]
Our little companion resting on our shoulder might look like a tiny robot, but he is our vigorous support in this journey. BD1 can help you zipline, open loot chests, scan hidden messages and provide you stem (health kits) at every crucial moment. Monitor him whenever he jumps from your shoulder, shows there’s a scannable object nearby. It provides interesting facts about the thing besides some extra XP.

[h1][b]😇Honest Rating:[/b][/h1]
I enjoyed my time with it, and you will too. Even though I am not a die-hard fan of Star Wars movies, as an amateur audience, I enjoyed each level providing me with thrill and immersive gameplay. I had time to experience this game throughout EA play, and I recommend the same to you. Traversing these stunning levels composed of high detailing was worth a while, and all this, along with a cute companion, made me super happy.

Rating: 9.5/10

This brings me back to the many story-driven LucasArts games of the late 90s and early 2000s. It captures the same plot interest and emotional investments that I had as a child and young adult. I'm actually impressed, because I really didn't think EA and Lucasfilm could pull it off. Man, was I proved wrong! Though I felt it was a little on the short side, I loved every minute. If they keep putting out stuff like this, I might end up liking the games more than the films in the end... well, better than the prequels and sequels at least. The last good Star Wars game was released a long time ago, in a galaxy far, far away! And boy were we starved for a good singleplayer game in this universe. I'm sure I'm not only speaking for myself.

This game delivers, provided you like some of the approaches and gameplay elements the developers went for. There might be some things you don't expect, such as:

- exploration in addition to platforming, a lot! Think of Uncharted 4 or the modern Tomb Raider games
- souls-like encounters with mobs of enemies as well as (mini-) bosses), loss of xp on death, enemy respawn
- and in addition to the above a skill-focused fight gameplay based on parry and deflection

The exploration, imho, is its own worth as it adds to the ancient lore of the Star Wars universe, but you are seldomly rewarded with truly relevant loot. Apart from healing stims this game will only give you cosmetic stuff.

Also the combat system lacks polish. For instance you cannot interupt animations and often fight against the camera in narrow spaces as much as you fight the enemies. Maybe this can later be mended by patches.

But for now this is the single best Star Wars game we got in a very long time. And I long for more! More singleplayer games, without crap like microtransactions and forced multiplayer. Yes I get it, games as a service are very lucrative. But please remember that there are so many great stories one could tell in this universe. That's what Star Wars is about. Please give Respawn Entertainment the time and ressources to make a sequel to this great game. Leave the rest to DICE I guess...

I bought this game earlier this year with pretty low expectations given how it was published by EA, which has a long history of ruining Star Wars games (or games in general for that matter).  However, my expectations for this game were totally wrong, and this ended up being the best game I played all year.  In fact, this is probably the best Star Wars game I have played in nearly two decades.

This game lets you play as a Jedi in hiding during the purges of the Jedi Order following Episode III.  Over the course of the game, you will be able to visit 7 different planets, some well known like Kashyyyk and Dathomir, and others not known.  Gameplay is a balanced mix of fighting, platforming, and puzzles.  Some people liken this game to a mix of Dark Souls, Tomb Raider, and Uncharted, although I have not personally played Uncharted to know how accurate this description is. In any case, I think they got the formula for the gameplay just right.  The game also features a fantastic storyline that is better than the new Star Wars movies in my opinion, and the music is also great.  Also, this game bucks the trend with EA and does not feature microtransactions or DLC of any kind.  

If you are on the fence about this game because you are wary of games published by EA, don’t worry.  If you are a fan of Star Wars, you will love this game.

Star Wars is a saga that I’ve often enjoyed for its games and its expanded universe, but that never stops disappointing me with its movies.
And so, this Fallen Order confirms it for me.

So, what about this game? The game starts with a good bit of staging during the tutorial. Then, as early as the 1st planet, you find yourself fairly frustrated, mainly because the game wants to be a metroidvania action-adventure (no, it’s not a souls-like, even though it borrows a few ideas). And so, exploration will be done through back-and-forth trips once the new abilities are acquired, which, in itself, could be a good idea, but really makes the beginning of the adventure nice but nothing more, which almost made me drop it. But once you get past a certain point, and once our Padawan gets his talents back, it simply becomes a real pleasure and finally gives that feeling of playing a Jedi like it rarely has been. I have to say the gameplay works rather well.

On the planets and exploration side, there are ideas, some good panoramas, but I find it still quite restrained considering what this franchise could bring, but it’s not a deal-breaker.

As for the story, well it will be like with the gameplay: the characters aren’t really charismatic (except BD-1 lol), but you end up letting yourself get pulled into the adventure. The big plus, in the end, of this story is that it makes us feel our character’s passage from Padawan to Jedi, and that part is successful.

Special mention to the music, which wonderfully picks up John Williams’ themes and makes them its own perfectly throughout the adventure.

Conclusion: this Fallen Order is a good, enjoyable game once you get past the first few slightly dull hours. You still end up getting attached to the characters, and the gameplay becomes a real pleasure: you really feel like you’re playing a Jedi, like it has rarely been done. For the price it costs during sales periods, clearly, it’s worth it.

[h1]I was never a Star Wars fan, but luckily Fallen Order doesn’t require you to be one.[/h1]

In 2010 then-president of EA said something about single-player games being “finished”. Here we are now with EA publishing one of the best and most successful single-player titles of 2019 under its wing.

Fallen Order tells an original story of Cal Kestis, an apprentice jedi hiding on a scrapyard planet called Bracca. Once he gets found by the Empire hunting the jedi and rescued by some strangers, he learns that the goal of his saviours is to restore the fallen Jedi Order. Having really no other place to go to, Cal agrees to help and embarks on a journey full of danger and failures, but also with a lot of soul-searching and new friends. 
The main advantage of the story is its characters. The main cast is not only always there for Cal, either just to chat about everyday things on the ship or to actually listen to his problems and be a genuine support on the journey, but they also impact the events of the game in a not-so direct way. Greez is being hunted by space gangsters which give you a hard time later, Cere [spoiler] is the former master of the main antagonist of the game [/spoiler]. 
Probably the most important character though, is our companion who is always there for us. Although the little droid, BD-1 doesn’t really say words, he communicates really well with Cal. The “dialogues” between the two form a very cool dynamic and really bond us with the two characters. 
Generally the writing of this game is amazing. The quieter moments with the crew members feel genuine and immersive. It’s this kind of absorbing story in which instead of saying “oh it’s a trap, nice”, you say “DAMN IT CAL IT’S AN OBVIOUS FU.CKING TRAP DON’T GO IN THERE PLEASE” 
[strike]Also, The Hot Goth Alien Cult Mommy.[/strike] 

In terms of gameplay, I'd say this is a softcore souls-like. An enemy that kills you takes your current xp and sends you back to your last meditation circle. To recover your xp you have to reach him again and hit him. Now it’s a cool attempt to make you more careful not to die and lose stuff, but it’s not really working. I was playing on second to hardest difficulty and honestly, I either did not care about the lost xp (it’s really easy and fast to farm back) or I just went and hit the guy that killed me not even because I wanted my experience back, but because he was just in the way. 
The combat is sweet. You can do parries and precision dodges or just roll around if you don’t feel comfortable with your timing. Low on health? Call out to BD to toss you a stim right into your hand. Fighting with your lightsaber lets you do a variety of moves such as throwing it at enemies or literally teleporting to them to close in on them faster. Your fancy glowstick also has a two-sided mode – it exceeds at fighting groups of enemies. It also has an attack in which you dual wield the glowstick and many players wish that this was a permanent mode. 
You can also use [i]The Force[/i]. In combat you can slow enemies down, pull them towards you or (my personal favorite, classic move) yeet them off a cliff (as a side note - many games have cocky enemies talking sh.it, and then get their asses floored seconds later, but hearing a clone yell “YOU ARE NOTHING COMPARED TO ME, JEDI" while falling down the abyss after getting yeeted off a cliff face is something else). Powers have many versions; a charged push can throw away multiple clones or even a big troll-thing. 
The Force is also used to solve many different environmental puzzles either to progress or to unlock a secret. Outside of combat you explore several places in the galaxy. You move around by climbing some plants, wall running, swinging on some vines, etc. Cal runs and jumps (man, hopping around was just so cool to me) around in a very intuitive way and it’s all incredibly animated. What I must say though, is that swimming overall feels very off and has some really bizarre animations. 
At first visit to some places the exploration feels really natural and immersive. I hardly ever got lost anywhere, even in the more open areas, and if I was ever in trouble, I could always use the map to see unexplored paths I had left. 
Unfortunately, backtracking to certain locations to get the leftover secrets and chests is an absolute disaster. Dathomir is a great planet, it’s a challenging, beautiful wasteland with cool lore and story. Going back to it and trying to reach the swamp area again is just a sh.itshow though. It’s so unnecessarily convoluted. It even seems like in this one place, past the bridge in the village should be an opening to just let you through. Instead, it’s blocked by this little wooden wall that you can’t jump over, so you must go around the whole location. It’s a serious flaw that is not only easily fixable, but just feels like somebody just forgot to put something there. 

The game looks very good and has some amazing landscapes. It also has a photo mode to play with. Regarding animation – most of them are amazing and very creative (BD tossing you heals is just so good). Besides swimming, the only complaint would be the lack of finisher animations. Some foes only have one and others get repetitive after a while. 

Now the sound design – maaan, this is [b]THE[/b] science fiction game. The space crafts flying around, blasters shooting, things exploding, funny glowsticks swinging around. They’re not only high quality and very characteristic, but they all just have the [b]oompff[/b] you know? The soundtrack amazingly complements the vibe. It’s very movie-like. What blew my mind is that if you listen to the OST album of this game on Spotify PC, it replaces the player bar with an extending lightsaber. How cool is that? 

I didn’t really encounter any technical issues, but what’s funny is that there is an infinite jumping glitch in the game that they did not patch. It’s not really that useful though, because you skip many invisible triggers while using it and it screws up the collision and map loading. It is funi. 

I was never a Star Wars fan. This is probably my first encounter with this franchise since Republic Commando on Xbox Classic or randomly seeing The Clone Wars on TV. Nothing wrong with the universe itself, I just never really got hooked by it. 
I was never a Star Wars fan, but luckily Fallen Order doesn’t require you to be one. It’s a wonderful adventure by itself. Maybe even a good starting point into the SW universe for a newbie like myself – and don’t get me wrong, I’m in no position to say that this is a good piece of the Star Wars media not knowing the rest of it. Nonetheless, from my experience with it, I can say that it’s enough to get you hooked on.

[h1] No Spoilers  [/h1]

At it's core Jedi Fallen Order feels like a mix between Souls like combat mixed with Tomb Raider climbing and exploration. The big difference tho is that unlike Dark Souls, here you can choose what difficulty you wish to play the game on.

[b] Difficulty [/b] affects 3 aspects of your gameplay, the timing for parry windows, the amount of damage you receive from enemies and how aggressive the enemies are. I made the mistake of choosing my difficulty to be Jedi Knight and the game felt way too easy, I only died 4 times in total of which 2 were from the first optional boss which I had no business on fighting that early and the last 2 deaths were on the final boss of the game. So I'd recommend starting your game with Jedi Master difficulty.
[b] The story [/b] of the game took me by surprise, after watching 2/3 of the new Star Wars movies I had literally no expectations for a decent story and just went into it for the lightsaber fights. I won't mention anything about the story in the spoiler free zone, but I just wanna note there are collectable items along the way which when you interact with will tell you a bit about the region/fights/people of the place you are currently visiting. Should you choose so you can also press esc to read a more detailed log of said event.
[b] Graphics  [/b] were beautiful even on medium settings, cutscenes were a huge highlight for me and in my 14 hour playthough I took 91 screenshots due to how gorgeous the visuals were. Even starting from the first mission I'm sure you will be impressed with it.
[b] Performance [/b] wise I had a decent number of micro stutters in gameplay and also in cutscenes. My PC specs are pretty bad, GPU is an Nvidia GTX 970 and CPU an Intel i5-6600K so that may be the case of the stutters in my case but I read online complaints from people with PCs far above mine having the same problem. Even with my 4-5 year old PC tho the game was extremely playable, stutters being a small inconvenience that didn't affect my fights negatively since they mostly happened while outdoors.

That is all I'd like to mention about the game without going into gameplay aspects some may not want to know before playing for themselves or mentioning specific missions/surprises that could be spoilers.

[h1] Spoilers [/h1]

From this point forward I'll talk freely about everything I liked and disliked about the game with every detail. If you want to have a blind experience going in it would be a good time to just press Play.

[b] Collectables [/b] in game were fine but I disliked how they were only cosmetics for your ligtsaber/poncho/suit/droid or ship. At some point in game you will get to a crash site and you will see a small rebel ship and a big star destroyer which you could have salvaged some parts from, that would have been awesome! But the devs just stuck with the crates that all look the same.
[b] The Skill Tree [/b] was pretty easy to fill, I ended my playthrough with everything unlocked except the longer saber throw range and the advanced aoe force push. In terms of usefulness It goes Survivability > Lightsaber > Force Powers.
[b] Characters [/b] were honestly the best I've seen in a Star Wars game, honestly rivaling The Mandalorian's cast imo. Even the Night Sister that joins you very late in the story was so well written, finally someone in the Star Wars universe that tells a droid that he doesn't understand it, she's like us!
[b] Combat [/b] in the game is pretty easy, you only have a few force spells, a block button, dodge and 2 buttons for lightsaber attacks. Once you unlock and upgrade force pull tho the light enemies could very well not be there since if you pull them the next hit insta kills them.
[b] RPG [/b] isn't a strong point of the game, you're not customizing how your character looks, making decisions for him, choosing a dark or a light path. This is the story of Cal Kestis and his journey, not a story of what you would do if you were in his role.
[b] Choices [/b] aren't really there in the game. Early on you will be able to choose a planet to go to, but in reality one of the planets is WAY harder than the one the game wants you to go to and also the progression is heavily cut off by the fact you can't double jump yet, making it impossible to finish the planet's story. The planet Dathomir is an early option just for you to get an early double sided lightsaber, not to actually progress the story.

[h1] Surprises [/h1]

These little or big surprises made me love the game even more, obviously they are scripted and just cause something is surprising it doesn't make it good, but I feel like this game did surprises in a VERY good way.

[b] Bosses [/b] will sometimes pop out of nowhere, you will just be taking a lift down in a random facility and then when the door opens suddenly it's the 2nd sister.  There are 4 optional bosses in the game that I have found. The Ooga Booga frog from the first planet (not the actual name), the white spider boss just jumps onto you while you're on your merry way of searching a body, the mini rancor looking creature from the ship wreck (I had no idea it was a boss since I literally fought 3 others like him outside his "cave"), and the alpha Dathomir creature.
[b] Bounty hunters [/b] will sometimes wait for you, blocking your path and starting a badass mini bossfight. The first one you encounter will also taser you and force you into a prison where you will have to cage fight while some bad ass alien music plays, it was epic!
[b] The FINAL boss [/b] literally doesn't have a health bar, that was THE most WTF and frightening thing I've seen in a non horror game.

[h1] Final Thoughts [/h1]

Jedi Fallen Order is a spark, a spark of hope that this is the quality of Star Wars games we will be getting from here on.
I pray Respawn will make Fallen Order 2 and maybe make it more RPG, letting us create our own character, be a padawan in the new order created by Master Kestis or maybe be a pure force user taught by Mother Merrin in an effort to try and revive the night sisters.
All we can do is hope this was the spark that will make the Star Wars franchise burn brighter than ever before.

Jedi: Fallen Order was a big refresher for me. Finally, we get a singleplayer Star Wars game that is based around lightsaber combat, and the idea to base it around From Software's style of combat was perfect in my opinion. It just works really well. I also consider this my big introduction to Star Wars. Before this game, I only watched the Disney-era of Star Wars movies, such as Force Awakens, Last Jedi, and Rise of Skywalker, which I watched a bit passively. I watched A New Hope a few years ago but it didn't hold my interest at the time. This game got me hooked into the world of Star Wars, and I did go back and watch the original trilogy (which I really enjoyed by the way, and Return of the Jedi was my favorite out of the OG trilogy).

[h1]Story[/h1]
The story is set 14 years before A New Hope and 5 years after Revenge of the Sith. The protagonist is Cal, a Jedi Padawan in hiding as a scavenger on Bracca. When he uses the Force to save a friend of his, this triggers the Force in an Inquisitor of the Galactic Empire, who comes to Bracca to hunt for the Jedi. After revealing himself as a Jedi and barely escaping the planet with the unexpected help of Cere and Greez, he adventures across the galaxy to save the Jedi Order and keep its secrets hidden from the Galactic Empire. 

In my opinion, it was a really strong story, and it helped peak my interest in Star Wars as a whole. The intro level on Bracca was strong, and the game never really lose its pace throughout the game, and even peaked again at the very end with a surprise appearance of a significant Star Wars character. It was a joy to play through. All the characters are well written and well voice acted (and acted, as some of the characters are real-life actors). Heck, even the Stormtrooper chatter is well written and voice acted too. 

Cal also has a great amount of customization, especially to his lightsaber, although I wish his outfit, BD-1, and the Mantis was a bit more customizible besides simple color swaps.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
As noted before, the gameplay is strong. Cal wields a lightsaber throughout the entire game, and uses a small amount of the Force (nothing like Force Unleashed). As stated earlier, the combat is based around From Software's style of combat, namely Sekiro. You can parry enemies, keep the pressure on them to break their parry and get hits on them, and block at the right time to do a big hit to their parry. You can also roll away to dodge unblockable attacks. I played a couple hours of Sekiro and I liked its combat, so the combat in Jedi Fallen Order was something I really enjoyed, and I'm glad they decided to base the combat around it. It works really well.

The boss fights in the game were great, especially the boss fights against another wielder of a lightsaber. It makes me wish there was more lightsaber combat outside of just boss fights. 

[h1]World and Visuals[/h1]
The world design of Jedi Fallen Order is great. It has that Star Wars look and vibe to it, and feels very big and open. It is accompanied by some great music that sound very appropriate for Star Wars. The game also is surprisingly a bit open world. The world has a lot of platforming, and Jedi temples with puzzles in them. The puzzles were well designed and a joy to figure out. The game runs on Unreal Engine 4, and looks beautiful, although I wish TAA wasn't the only antialiasing on offer, as I never really been a fan of it personally. It is possible to disable TAA in the game's ini files but it messes up the hair in the game, so I just put up with it. I played through the entire game in 1440p Medium-High Settings at about 70-80 FPS and it looked fantastic, although there were some heavy frame drops when the game was trying to seamlessly load new areas. The lack of loading screens at all was great, but the frame drops could get pretty annoying.

[h1]Negatives[/h1]
While I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone remotely interested, there were some weak points.

[b]The lock-on camera works, but it can constantly switch between people in fights[/b], and when you're fighting about 4 Stormtroopers at once, it can get pretty frustrating. I think it's because switching targets is bound to right stick on the controller, and if you barely give it a love tap, it switches targets. It can throw you off and get you hit constantly. 

[b]The game starts off difficult, but as Cal grows in power and gains abilities, the game becomes a lot easier.[/b] I played the game on Jedi Master, and while the game at the start was a challenge, once I got more abilities, got more health and force, found more stimpacks, [spoiler]and found the double-bladed lightsaber[/spoiler], the game became a lot less challenging. While it feels good to be a powerful Jedi, the stress of the early-game difficulty was almost gone completely. I'm not sure if this is normal for From Software-esque games or not.

[b]I ran into a few quirks and bugs[/b]. It was small stuff, like the camera freaking out, one enemy not attacking me at all, and floating in mid-air during locked animations in combat. Some of the bugs were pretty jarring. For example, I fell through the world on Zeffo and fell forever, forcing me to quit to title screen and load my previous save. 

[b]Fully completing all worlds is a chore and can get really frustrating,[/b] I decided to do this since I was wanting to have all the customization options at my disposal, and it took forever. Also, sometimes the area is only accessible if you trek through all the enemies and world before it again, as sometimes you go through a one-way exit of the area and can't go back. Sometimes the game grants shortcuts to these areas, but not all of them.

[b]Once you beat the game and collect everything, that's pretty much it.[/b] There's no side quests, no New Game Plus, and no extra endgame content. Once you beat the game, that's it. You're free to explore previous worlds, but that's about it. Hopefully this means future expansions to new planets. Also, please add New Game Plus. It would be cool to play this game on Grandmaster with a fully-maxed out Cal. 

[h1]Summary[/h1]
Despite all the negatives I have with this game, it is a really good game, and you should play it. Hopefully there are expansions to new planets, and there is a sequel to this game. Maybe the sequel could be a more open world game based around your own Jedi Padawan made with a character creator who is trained by Cal and Cere, or something like that. Please keep this series alive!

With the release of [I]Star Wars Jedi: Survivor[/I] being just around the corner, I decided to dust off [I]Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order – Deluxe Edition[/I] from my backlog and give it a go. [I]Fallen Order[/I] is a Soulslike Metroidvania action-adventure game that was influenced by the popular [I]Dark Souls[/I] games and the [I]Tomb Raider[/I] Survivor Trilogy. If you’re a fan of these games (and presumably also a fan of [I]Star Wars[/I]), chances are you’ll enjoy [I]Fallen Order[/I] to some degree.

[I]Fallen Order[/I] is a great game. I grew up playing the [I]Star Wars Jedi Knight[/I] game series, so it’s hard for me not to compare this game with great titles like [I]Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II[/I] and [I]Jedi Outcast[/I]. There’s great emphasis on lightsaber combat in [I]Fallen Order[/I], giving players more control over lightsaber offensive and defensive moves. It’s very gratifying and empowering to manually deflect each blaster bolt at the press of a button in [I]Fallen Order[/I] than to have it done passively for you as in the older games.

Players also get to visit multiple planets, each with its own unique terrain and colour palette. You start off at a scrapyard planet that serves as the tutorial level, then you’re whisked off to one with mesas and seemingly bottomless canyons. This is followed by a planet with snow-capped peaks and caves, then one of lush forests disturbed by lifeless Imperial structures, before landing on a planet with a hellish landscape that fills you with dread. The meticulously designed and rendered locales in [I]Fallen Order[/I] are simply awe-inspiring, and are inviting for thorough exploration.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2945199088
That being said, the individual gameplay elements – while praiseworthy – don’t complement each other all that well. Specifically, I found the Soulslike combat system and the [I]Tomb Raider[/I]-esque adventuring/exploration at odds with each other. Soulslike are meant to be difficult, but rewarding with perseverance and learning. To create opportunities to learn from mistakes, enemies respawn when you recover health and Force power by resting at save/meditation points. The idea is that with full health and Force, you are well-equipped to fight more enemies, thus having more chances to hone your fighting skills, and to earn more skill points to improve your Force, Lightsaber and Survival abilities.

This Soulslike combat gameplay works just fine. Yet, with over 300 collectibles (Force Echoes, Life and Force Essences, cosmetics chests, stim/health canisters, scans, encrypted logs, and plant seeds) scattered across the planets you’ll visit, searching for these items gets tedious quickly when you have to fight the same, respawned enemies multiple times. Plus, there is no Fast Travel (even [I]Dark Souls[/I] games allow warping between bonfires/save points), which just makes adventuring/exploring extra tiresome. With the story directing you to revisit planets so you can explore previously unreachable places, adventuring in [I]Fallen Order[/I] feels more of a chore than play.

Storywise, [I]Fallen Order[/I] is…okay. You play as Cal Kestis, a Padawan who went into hiding after the events of Order 66. When the Inquisitorius were alerted to his whereabouts, he finds himself on a quest to recover a holocron containing a list of Force-sensitive younglings in efforts to restore the Jedi Order. A major problem with [I]Star Wars[/I] stories like this, set between the events of the prequels and the original trilogy, is that many fans already know what the big picture outcome is. It’s not exactly spoilers here, but we know Cal will not restore the Jedi Order. Thus, for next 20 hours or so, you’re literally chasing a MacGuffin that has no impact on the [I]Star Wars[/I] lore.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2945199404
So, how is [I]Fallen Order[/I] a great game given my complaints? Because in spite of its flaws, [I]Fallen Order[/I] oozes with [I]Star Wars[/I] atmosphere. The intense lightsaber action, the detailed and near photorealistic environments, and the wonderful John Williams-esque score work cohesively to immerse you in the fantastical galaxy. But, it’s the characters that make [I]Fallen Order[/I] special. Cal’s moments with them, especially his droid companion BD-1, flesh out their motivations, sins, regrets, and vulnerabilities. (One side character – arguably the best one aside from BD-1 – feels like a late addition to the crew as a deus ex machina, but should have been introduced earlier to act as Cal’s foil to allow for better character and plot development.) The actors did a fantastic job in their motion capture and vocal performances, too.

If you enjoy poring over special features on movie DVDs/Blu-Rays, I think the Deluxe Edition may interest you. I found the 1.5 hours of documentaries fascinating, but hardly worth a re-watch. The digital artbook offers a look into how character, vehicle and environment designs evolved. (Sadly, the documentaries and artbook can only be viewed in-game.) The Deluxe Edition also comes with cosmetic items like “premium content” lightsaber parts, clothing, as well as skins for BD-1 and your ship, all of which serve no other purpose than to change how things look. Aside from using one “premium content” part to customize my lightsaber, I didn’t use any of the Deluxe Edition cosmetic items.

As someone who has not played a brand new [I]Star Wars[/I] game since 2003, I’ve truly enjoyed the challenging lightsaber combat, great side characters, and immersion that [I]Fallen Order[/I] offers. Sure, it could have benefitted from better co-implementation of the action and adventuring gameplay, but it’s just so fun overall. And because this game series shows such potential, I’ve become more excited and curious about [I]Star Wars Jedi: Survivor[/I] than before. I think you’ll understand what I mean once you’ve given [I]Fallen Order[/I] a try. Though it may not be the best [I]Star Wars[/I] game there is, it’s certainly one of the better ones.

Can't really say i'm a SW fan or anything, but what i can say is this game was totally awesome and definitely a step in the right direction for EA!

The story was pretty good, and had some of the coolest moments i experienced in recent memory (again, i haven't even seen most of the movies and i was still able to enjoy it), most of the characters were also pretty cool & memorable, i really liked Cal as the protagonist and found him to be pretty interesting & fun to play as, and of course BD-1 is one of of the best videogame companions period :P
(i especially love how there is an actual button on the controller for you to check on him and make sure he's doing alright, more games need to do that!)

The graphics are beautiful and it runs fine most of the time (but the game does suffer from random frame drops and hiccups so you should probably keep that in mind), i also didn't face any major bugs or glitches.

The combat is Dark Soul inspired, but not nearly as hard or punishing (it can still be quite challenging compared to normal games, especially on higher difficulties.), combine that with how cool and fun the lightsabers are to use, and the Uncharted/Tomb Raider inspired set pieces and you end up with a pretty good and fun gameplay loop.
(You can fully customize your own light saber, big +++)

Side note: if you ever felt the game wasn't as good as it could've been when you're just starting out, it most definitely does get a lot better the more you play, in both combat (once you unlock all moves, some of which i thought you should've started with, or at least unlocked a lot sooner) and the story (can't comment on that sadly cuz spoilers :P)

The open world was fine, you have multiple unique planets to explore, each as a separate mini-hub full of various collectibles to collect, shortcuts to unlock and unique bosses/mini bosses to fight (i'm not the biggest fan of open world busywork so i didn't even bother with getting all the collectibles, but they weren't too excessive or annoying i guess)
you can even explore underwater locations later in the game and those were also fine considering how hard it is to make good underwater levels.

Now the bad:
Some animations weren't as good as you'd expect from an AAA game, some sliding/jumping sections were a bit annoying to get right, backtracking was tedious at times since there is no fast travel between rest locations but it wasn't anything  too excessive i guess, the game also refused to launch altogether for me with the new EA launcher, and only worked with the old origin launcher.

As you can see the good far outweighs the minor cons i just mentioned, but still, this is definitely not a perfect game by any means, they still have a lot of room for improvements and polish in so many aspects, so don't play this expecting something great/perfect, but more like something that's actually good and fun.
After all, what really matters and what made me feel like i had to leave this one a positive review was the fact that it was "FUN", with some great story moments, interesting & memorable side characters and enjoyable lightsaber combat. 8/10

Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order is hands-down one of the best Star Wars games in recent times. Do you remember when was the last time we had a good Star Wars game before Jedi Fallen Order ? Exactly. It was a long time ago in a galaxy far far away. But now after many many years, the developer Respawn Entertainment, the veteran development team of the original Call of Duty, Titanfall and Apex Legends has LITERALLY revived or respawned Star Wars game back to its purely single player action adventure glory days. Yes, you heard it. No microtransactions, no lootboxes, no gotcha mechanics. Just pure character driven story, gameplay and exploration that we all know and love about Star Wars.

The game's strongest points are story, characters, combat, soundtrack and environmental level design. Respawn Entertainment has once again crafted an intricately detailed and excellently crafted world for us to explore where you can traverse, explore and backtrack various planets and fight all varieties of enemies and monsters. From local creatures to bounty hunters to imperial troops and beyond, there's a large selection of enemies in the game that'll challenge your skill in combat. 

The game's story links to the Star Wars movies, specifically after Star Wars Episode III and the infamous Order 66 and the purge of the Jedis. You are Cal Kestis, a Jedi on the run being hunted by the Imperial Inquisitors. Your mission is to save the future generation of Jedi by finding the location of potential force users. You travel around several planets with the help of your friends trying to survive, gather allies and intel to fight back the empire while trying to achieve your mission. You will along the way face the many foes of the empire who's trying to stop you from achieving your goal. When you're immersed in the story, you really do feel like you're on a grand adventure / quest with an sense of fear and ever present danger on the horizon.

The game's combat is primarily focused on melee lightsaber combat. There's a decent varieties of force powers to choose from as well. Once you master the combat and combine your lightsaber and force abilities, you will truly feel like a Jedi Master as you strike down your enemies one after another. The combat itself can be very challenging depending on your skill and difficulty, which you can adjust on the fly. Think Dark Souls / Sekiro with adjustable difficulty settings. It is very satisfying and rewarding.

I do have to mention the characters in the game. Both heroes and villains are VERY WELL crafted, even down to normal enemies like stormtroopers who will chatter with others in the background and react to your actions. All the characters in the game have personalities, feels authentic in a true Star Wars universe and have their own stories to tell. The soundtrack is also very authentic to Star Wars as well. Very well done.

And when you combine the well crafted story, pulse pounding combat, endearing characters and grandiose Star Wars soundtrack with the excellent level design, you get one heck of a good Star Wars game. The game is also decently lengthy too averaging at 25 to 30 hours depending on how you play and how much you explore. It also has a New Game+ mode for added replay value.

With all that said, I give Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order a solid 9/10. For Star Wars fans, you've already bought and played the game. For the rest of you, if you're on the edge, this game is a definite winner and is absolutely worth your money. Not only is it an excellent Star Wars game but its also a great single player third person action adventure game too. This game has potential for a trilogy and I do hope EA let Respawn Entertainment make it.

It feels like you’re really in the Star Wars universe, taking on Stormtroopers and uncovering secrets. Overall, it’s a great experience that keeps you hooked!
