Let's just start by saying that yes, I'm down voting a VERY popular, very well regarded triple-A title.  I get it.  A lot of people love it.  I'm not saying they're wrong.  But it's a miss for me.  I can explain why, and I will.

In fact, I can do it pretty succinctly:  it's not what I expected.  I expected something like Shadows of Mordor or the Batman Arkham City games where there was lots of reflex combat except that you got to swing a lightsaber around and fight stormtroopers and stuff because, hey, the sound of a lightsaber is EXTREMELY cool and Star Wars is awesome.  This is the type of game play that all the advertising highlights.  And I got some of that.  What I didn't expect was "Tomb Raider, except you're a Jedi."  Not that there's anything wrong with Tomb Raider.  I LOVE the Tomb Raider series.  Both the originals and the reboots.  It's just a matter of balance.  Tomb Raider is about solving puzzles with a little bit of combat.  And that's fine if that's what you're in the mood for.  But Star Wars sets a different mood.  "Wars" is right there in the title, you expect the puzzles to take a back seat to the combat.  I never saw Obi Wan futzing around trying to figure out how to use the Force to make a fan stop so he could jump to a ledge, then shimmy along it to pull a lever to open a trap door... etc. and so forth... and until I finally lost interest I felt like I was doing far too much of that kind of thing and not nearly enough deflecting blaster bolts from stormtroopers.  

The intro / tutorial blew me away.  The story, the music, the character, it all seemed like it was going a good place.  I was grinning ear-to-ear thinking "now THIS is a Star Wars story!"  But once I got into the meat of it the pace just seemed to grind to a halt.  Now I'm trying to figure out how to get to certain parts of the map and wondering if I'm just missing something or maybe that's something I'm supposed to come back to later after I've pulled a lever somewhere else, and occasionally slaughtering little animals, and meeting characters that weren't all that interesting.  I'm old school Star Wars when R2D2 was as cute as it got.  Then they introduced BB8, who was R2 but with more cute.  I don't remember the droids name from the game but forget BB8, because this guy is New and Improved with Even MORE Cute!!!! He rides around on your back which is just adorable and explains from a game standpoint how he can stay with you while you do all the crazy wall running and jumping and stuff which might not bother a lot of people but I just had a hard time feeling like a Jedi with a cute little droid stuck to my back all the time.  The other characters on my crew hinted at fascinating back stories but in the present just didn't seem like people I really cared to get to know.  And the crafting?  Why does every game feel the need to jam crafting in one way or the other when it seems mostly pointless.  Sure, it's very cool that I can change the color and maybe even the sound of my blade, but who the heck cares if there are tons of different options to change tiny details of the handle when the only time I can really see that is on the crafting screen itself?  Just seems like a lot of misdirected effort to me.

I've been wrong before.  Sometimes I'll go back and play a game that didn't keep my attention and suddenly say "oh, I get it now!"  It's often like that with games that are well reviewed but that I just couldn't get excited about.  But I got through the tutorial episode (which... again... was awesome) and then started digging into the story, and after my 3 hours or so of play time I just kind of lost any interest in continuing.

[h1][b]**Please Note**[/b][/h1]
[i]Is this a fun game? Yeah, it is. However, I don’t know if I would personally suggest for others to pick up the game, especially at $60. [u]If you want a [b]TL;DR[/b], scroll down to the bottom[/u][/i]


[h1][b][u]Opening Thoughts[/u][/b][/h1]
I mean, it's just my opinion but as fun as certain elements of the game were, I think it’s seriously hampered by a handful of design choices that prevent me from recommending this game, especially at the retail price of $60.


[h1][u][b]Game Design: [i]Replay Value[/i][/b][/u][/h1]
For example, there’s no New Game Plus, which hurts the replay value. Therefore, you’re mostly going to unlock the same skills and play the same missions and access the same secret areas in almost the same order every time. Especially considering that you can’t access certain skills until later in the game, it means that it’s kind of easy to over-level and unlock the same skills you do with each playthrough. Some people don't agree with the concept of a New Game Plus, and to them, I just want to ask: what's the point of replaying the game on a harder difficulty? Do you get something different or experience the game in a radically different way? Not everyone needs this replay value but this game doesn't add much to the gaming experience with multiple playthroughs.


[h1][u][b]Game Design: [i]Looting/Unlockables/Puzzles[/i][/b][/u][/h1]
I also didn’t care for the loot system where almost every single upgrade was a paint job for yourself, BD-1, the Mantis, or the lightsaber. I mean, it’s fun to customize the lightsaber with a custom grip, sleeve, button, and hilt. It’s just that none of it affects gameplay. It doesn’t affect damage/stats, or the amount of force power you have. Chasing after crates are fairly mundane unless you get the upgrade carry-amount for stim packs. I found myself growing annoyed that I spent several minutes exploring puzzle areas off the beaten path only to be rewarded with a new paint job for the Mantis.

I'd even argue that some ([b]not all[/b]) the puzzle designs are not as intuitive as the game intends. One specific puzzle involving candles/water wasn't very well explained, even with in-game hints to the point the player in the right direction. I don't consider myself bad with puzzles but even then, I felt that some of the designs were overly complicated for their simplistic solutions.


[h1][u][b]Game Design: [i]Enemies & Combat[/i][/b][/u][/h1]
For a Star Wars game that emulated more of [b]Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice[/b] than any other Dark Souls game in recent memory, there weren’t that many enemies. I want to live out the fantasy of being a Jedi-on-the-run and for some reason, the world while having some enemies, in a few sections of the game it did feel rather empty and more focused on the puzzles. Also, being able to parry didn’t feel as rewarding, especially considering it didn’t always interrupt enemy attack patterns. I was better off dodging 95% of the time.

Finally, why aren’t all meditation spots in useful areas like before a boss fight? Sure, there were a few spots that had one before a boss fight, but there were a few instances, especially in the early game where sometimes it took 40-80 seconds of running, climbing, & jumping just to get back to where you were. If you’re going to play this game for the first time, regardless of whatever souls/sekiro games you’ve played in the past, don’t start on the hardest difficulty. The checkpoints will become frustrating and it’ll be better to learn the game concept on more forgiving difficulties. There also isn't a fast travel system, meaning you have to run from one end of the map to the other repeatedly. The first time I did it, I was fine with this; I was able to explore and see more of the world. The 5th time? Not so much.


[h1][u][b]Final Thoughts/Story[/b][/u][/h1]
At least the story and general combat are enjoyable; I enjoyed some of the set pieces and Cal Kestis (& BD-1!) is a fun character to follow around. There were some phenomenal moments that made me really happy I was visiting the Star Wars universe and this game did scratch that itch. The story is a bit light and while it's not perfect, I think it was suitable for the narrative they wanted to share. I just don’t get why everyone is giving a pass to this game when it failed (imo) several other aspects of basic game design. The game may not be an RPG, but it has the trappings of one when it implements elements found in other games like Dark Souls, Sekiro, & DMC.


[h1][b]**TL;DR**[/b][/h1]
[list]
    [*][b]Is it a fun game? Yes.[/b]
    [*][b]Does it have features and game design consistent with other $60 single-player games? In my opinion, no. I think that some players are giving this game a pass on those problems because it’s the first competent Star Wars game we’ve received in a while.[/b]
[/list]
